undervalued.faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
undervalued.faq.subtitle: What you need to know about our DCF calculator
undervalued.faq.q1: How is the 'Intrinsic Value' calculated in this table?
undervalued.faq.a1: We use the Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) mathematical model. Our bot extracts the actual Operating Cash Flow and Capital Expenditures (CapEx) from each company to obtain its pure Free Cash Flow (FCF). We then project that money into the future using conservative growth rates and discount it back to its present value.
undervalued.faq.q2: What exactly does 'Margin of Safety' mean?
undervalued.faq.a2: It is the percentage difference between the current stock price and our calculated intrinsic value. A green margin of 30% means the stock is selling 30% cheaper than what it's mathematically worth, representing a 'cushion' of protection and a potential buying opportunity.
undervalued.faq.q3: Why do some very famous companies appear overvalued (red)?
undervalued.faq.a3: A negative margin indicates that the stock is expensive compared to the cash it generates today. Many tech companies trade at high prices because the market speculates they will earn much more in the future. Our model is conservative, so it tends to punish high speculation.
undervalued.faq.q4: How often is the data updated?
undervalued.faq.a4: Our database is 100% automated. A script reads the information directly from Yahoo Finance and syncs it to the cloud every hour. Prices, outstanding shares, and accounting reports are kept up to date without manual intervention.
undervalued.faq.q5: If a stock has a large green margin, should I buy it?
undervalued.faq.a5: Definitely not blindly! The DCF calculator is the best starting point, but it's just math. Before investing, you should use this data as an initial filter and then do your own research: analyze if the company has too much debt, how its management is, and if it has a real competitive advantage (Moat).
undervalued.faq.q6: Why do all companies have a default 10% growth and discount rate?
undervalued.faq.a6: That 10% is just a standardized mathematical baseline to give you a quick overview of the market. However, this table is an interactive calculator: you are invited to freely modify the 'Growth' and 'Discount' boxes for each company according to your own risk criteria and analysis to obtain a truly personalized intrinsic value.
